text.p: AO Yuganskneftegaz crude oil output will decline to 25.2 million tonnes in 1997, Interfax news agency quoted Sergei Muravlenko, president of NK YUKOS oil holding company as saying on Monday.
YUKOS in late December estimated that 1996 output for its Yuganskneftegaz production unit would be 26.38 million tonnes and that 1997 output would be 24.60 tonnes.
Muravlenko also said on Monday that 1997 sales for all of YUKOS would be 20.4 trillion roubles, the agency quoted him as saying. YUKOS has not released 1996 financial results.
Muravlenko said that YUKOS would export 11.8 million tonnes of crude oil and 3.8 million tonnes of refined oil products worth $1.232 billion and $446 million respectively.
In December YUKOS estimated crude oil exports for 1996 would be 8.02 million tonnes for the group.

Interfax also quoted him as saying YUKOS would refine 21.66 million tonnes of oil, a 17.3 percent increase on 1996 levels. In December YUKOS estimated it would refine 18.46 million tonnes for the whole of 1996.

The agency also quoted Muravlenko as saying that YUKOS production unit AO Samaraneftegaz would produce eight million tonnes of oil in 1997, as estimated in December, bringing total YUKOS production to 33.2 million tonnes this year.
YUKOS, one of about a dozen integrated oil companies established during Russian economic reforms, is the country's third-largest oil group by output.
